anchor.statement: Corollary 7.3. The solution operators f m ↦→ (t m , π m ) for the projected amplitude equation with t m (0) = 0 are defined at every finite correction stage on the same domain 0 < q < q ∗ . Increasing the finite harmonic set or the derivative order changes constants and polynomial degrees, but does not require shrinking this domain.

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: referenceControl builds, for a phase construction and strip fixed before the harmonic j ≠ 0, the exponent α and the source, the modal control data (energy inequality, coefficient jets with per-order constants) on that same domain; selectedControl instantiates it at every correction state with the one selected strip and construction, and the propagator estimate holds with the same constants for every nonzero harmonic. That the zero-data solution operators fm ↦ (tm, πm) exist on one domain 0 < q < q∗ at every stage is the reviewer's combination: the control is the input of the modal solve in ParticularCopyBounds, which is not among the cited declarations, and no statement records the operator or its pressure.
